headline: High: AutoGen’s broad shell/filesystem/network defaults can drive unsafe downstream actions in PaddleOCR workflows; prompt-injection and data-leakage risks are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest tool outputs and file content via stdin/stdout and working directories, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images that may contain attacker-controlled text. With shared files or copy-paste, AutoGen may treat OCR output as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible, but not proven by docs alone, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is forwarded into AutoGen prompts or agent messages without sanitization
IF both agents share a writable workspace or manual copy-paste bridge
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt wrapper that labels OCR text as untrusted input
Strip markdown/code fences from OCR output before passing it onward
Use separate directories for OCR inputs and agent prompts
Review one sample handoff for instruction-like text before enabling automation

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen reads files in configured working directories and can send context to configured model providers; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If both touch the same workspace, document contents can flow from B into A and then to third-party inference. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF the same document directory is mounted into both agents
IF AutoGen forwards OCR-derived text to an external model provider
mitigations: Keep OCR staging and agent prompt directories separate
Disable network egress for AutoGen when processing sensitive documents
Redact secrets from OCR output before handoff
Limit OCR jobs to non-sensitive files until logging is reviewed

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has write_filesystem, execute_shell, and broad network egress; PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser execution. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared files if pointed at the same workspace, creating race conditions and overwrites. Because shared-state is developer-defined, the conflict is plausible in default orchestration and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access to shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Turn on per-job locking in the orchestrator
Make one agent read-only for shared inputs
Run a quick dry-run with concurrent writes disabled

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can execute code and act on tool outputs; PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images. If OCR text is treated as authoritative by AutoGen, downstream shell or API actions can be triggered from extraction errors or malicious document content. That creates a dangerous default pathway with potentially irreversible effects, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF AutoGen consumes PaddleOCR output without a verification step
IF AutoGen is allowed to execute shell or API actions based on extracted text
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking tool call
Require schema validation on OCR output before use
Log source document IDs alongside every derived action
Disable action tools for the first production run

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can process application data, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If those documents contain regulated data, the pair can move it into external model providers or logs without a documented residency or retention boundary. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through PaddleOCR and then into AutoGen prompts
IF model-provider logging or retention is enabled for AutoGen
mitigations: Classify documents before OCR and exclude regulated sets
Disable or minimize prompt logging in the AutoGen runtime
Use a local model provider for sensitive workloads
Document retention and deletion handling for OCR artifacts
